question:
(a) Two beams of light have the same frequency above threshold frequency but different intensities. Compare the photoelectric current and maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons in the two cases.
(b) Explain why this comparison is not explained by wave theory.

options.A:
(a) For the same frequency above threshold, the more intense beam produces greater photoelectric current because it supplies more photons per second; both beams give the same $K_{\max}$ because $K_{\max}=h\nu-\phi_0$.
(b) Wave theory would expect greater intensity to give greater electron energy, contrary to observation.
options.B:
(a) Both photoelectric current and $K_{\max}$ are greater for the more intense beam.
(b) Wave theory predicts the same result.
options.C:
(a) The more intense beam gives the same current but smaller $K_{\max}$.
(b) Wave theory cannot explain photon momentum.
options.D:
(a) Neither current nor $K_{\max}$ depends on intensity.
(b) Wave theory predicts no photoelectric effect.
